gen-dafont-over-there-poppins: Poppins reads tall and sturdy, its curves running loose with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye. Over There adds a vintage-military voice up top, with generous gaps between letters.
gen-dafont-ozone-fs-bespoke-serif: Ozone draws every stem and crossbar at a single thickness, like a stylus held at fixed pressure. Bespoke Serif follows with dignified bowls that thin gracefully, giving the pair an authority the heading alone lacks.
gen-dafont-ozone-fs-sentient: Sentient reads sophisticated, with pinched, closed-in apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than its stems. Ozone, geometric and technical, keeps its round forms open and wide, and that open-versus-closed tension is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-pixel-operator-fs-literata: Pixel Operator sets fixed-width, code-style letters whose terminals never close in, so words land as solid blocks. Literata's text serif body has stems just heavier than its hairlines.
gen-dafont-pixel-operator-rubik: Retro terminal energy, all fixed-width blocks and open line ends. Rubik takes over below in a soft sans-serif with big lowercase, while Pixel Operator earns its place in big, short lines.
gen-dafont-prime-manrope: Prime hangs its bulky lowercase like clothespins on a line, with stroke weight that shifts noticeably but never dramatically. And Manrope, a sans with bright open curves and a minimal step up to capitals, feels friendlier and lighter beside those closed letters.
gen-dafont-prime-satoshi: Stroke weight that shifts noticeably yet never dramatically gives Prime its approachable, slightly bulky look. Satoshi, a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, sits beside it like a lighter, brighter cousin.
gen-dafont-prime-work-sans: Prime has a light swell in each bowl, like pressed glass, and its closed letters look bulky and friendly. And Work Sans, with c tips that never creep toward touching, suits being sized a little smaller than you might expect.
gen-dafont-quark-fs-bespoke-slab: Quark is a sans-serif with a spacious c and strokes that never vary from stem to terminal. Bespoke Slab's tall serif lowercase gives the pair its grounded, refined weight.
gen-dafont-quark-fs-literata: Quark's strokes hold flat from stem to terminal, with no contrast at all. Its geometric, technical lines suit headings, while Literata's classic serif shape, sturdy thin lines and wide, unclosed mouths, carries the bookish, sophisticated text.
